'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb]] (AQIM) names [[Algeria]]n [[Islamism|Islamist]] Abu Obaida Yusuf al-Annabi as its new leader, following the death of [[Abdelmalek Droukdel]] during the [[Battle of Talahandak]] in June. Al-Annabi has been on the [[United States|U.S.]] "international terrorist" blacklist since September 2015, and he has regularly appeared in jihadist propaganda videos. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/22/al-qaeda-in-north-africa-appoints-leader-to-replace-droukdel (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**[[Battle of Mekelle (2020)]]
***[[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Ethiopian Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] issues an ultimatum to the leaders of the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]], giving the group 72 hours to surrender before [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|federal forces]] begin a ground offensive to capture the region's capital [[Mekelle]]. The Ethiopian military says Mekelle will be "encircled" and "shown no mercy". [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/22/ethiopian-military-warns-mekelle-civilians-ahead-of-assault-on-city (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rajasthan]]
*****[[Rajasthan]] reports 3,260 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began and bringing the total confirmed cases in the state to 243,936. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/jaipur/rajasthan-reports-3260-covid-19-cases-17-deaths/articleshow/79353683.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] reports 490 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO66534700S0A121C2AC8000 (''Nihon Keizai Shimbun'')]
****[[Japan]] surpasses 2,000 total [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] deaths. [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2020112200247/japan-coronavirus-deaths-exceed-2-000.html (Nippon.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports 59 new deaths in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since July and bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,662. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/pakistan/pakistan-reports-59-more-covid-19-deaths-toll-rises-to-7662/articleshow/79350323.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The [[Government of South Korea|government]] will increase [[social distancing]] rules in the [[Seoul Capital Area]] to Level 2 and both [[North Jeolla Province|North]] and [[South Jeolla Province]] to Level 1.5 beginning November 24 amidst a third wave of COVID-19 cases. In level 2, gatherings involving more than 100 people are banned, some high-risk facilities will be closed, and restaurants cannot operate dine-in services after 9:00 p.m.. Cafes and coffee shops are only allowed to offer takeout and delivery services. Also, indoor sports facilities must close at 9:00 p.m.. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20201122002400320 (Yonhap News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]], [[COVID-19 testing]]
**** The [[Dubai Health Authority]] (DHA) begins to introduce saliva tests to detect active COVID-19 infections in children between the ages of 3 and 16 in all DHA facilities and DHA-run screening centers across [[Emirate of Dubai|Dubai]]. These tests are more than 90% accurate, making them a viable alternative to nasal swab tests which are uncomfortable and harder to use to test children. [https://gulfnews.com/uae/health/dubai-introduces-new-saliva-test-to-detect-covid-19-in-kids-1.75428919 (''Gulf News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France|French]] [[Government of France|authorities]] orders the culling of 1,000 minks in the [[Eure-et-Loir]] region after lab analyses detected a mutated version of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in one farm. All animal products in that farm will be destroyed. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/france-mink-coronavirus-mutation-b1759977.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]] states that [[Spain]] will begin a comprehensive COVID-19 [[vaccination]] programme in January and expects to have vaccinated a substantial part of the population within three months. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201122-spain-plans-to-begin-vaccination-programme-in-january-pm-sanchez (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports 6,017 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new record for the second consecutive day and bringing the nationwide total to 446,882 cases. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/turkeys-covid-19-numbers-record-levels-day-74346907 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[South Australia]] further eases restrictions imposed earlier in the week, ending a stay at home order but maintaining limits on public and private gatherings and quotas at businesses.  [https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/world/2020/11/covid-19-australia-further-eases-coronavirus-restrictions-as-infections-dwindle.html (Newshub)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports 1,584 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new one-day record since the pandemic began and highest number of daily cases on Sunday than any other [[Provinces and territories of Canada|provinces and territories]]. [https://edmonton.ctvnews.ca/alberta-reports-more-covid-19-cases-on-sunday-than-any-other-province-1.5200077 (CFRN-DT)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] public health officials announces a suspension of outdoor dining at restaurant for three-weeks starting from November 25 at 10:00{{nbsp}} p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] due to rise of new infections in the [[United States|U.S.]] largest county. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-11-22/l-a-county-suspends-outdoor-dining-at-restaurants-as-coronavirus-surges (''Los Angeles Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2020 G20 Riyadh summit]]
**World leaders at the [[G20]] summit in [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]], close the summit with calls for a coordinated response to the [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] pandemic and support for vaccinations for everyone. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/g20-saudi-arabia-riyadh-coroanvirus-pandemic/2020/11/22/5d909c0a-2a81-11eb-9c21-3cc501d0981f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-g20-saudi-communique-covid-idUSKBN2820KF (Reuters)]
*The [[United States]] withdraws from the [[Treaty on Open Skies]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/22/united-states-formally-withdraws-from-open-skies-treaty (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mayfair Mall shooting]]
**Several people are arrested, including a 15-year-old boy, in connection with Friday's [[mass shooting]] at the [[Mayfair Mall]] in [[Wauwatosa, Wisconsin]], which injured eight people. The shooting followed an altercation between two groups, according to police. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/15-year-old-arrested-wisconsin-mall-shooting-injured-eight-n1248568 (NBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Faisal Mekdad]] is appointed as [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates (Syria)|Foreign Minister of Syria]], succeeding [[Walid Muallem]], who died last Monday. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/syria-appoints-veteran-diplomat-faisal-mekdad-foreign-minister (VoA)]
*[[2020 Burkinabé general election]]
**Voters in [[Burkina Faso]] head to the polls in an election marred by a dramatic surge of [[Terrorism in Burkina Faso|terrorist attacks]] within the recent years. Incumbent President [[Roch Marc Christian Kaboré]] of the [[People's Movement for Progress]] seeks another term while he is challenged by two main opponents, [[Zéphirin Diabré]] of the [[Union for Progress and Reform]] and Eddie Komboïgo of the [[Congress for Democracy and Progress]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/burkina-faso-votes-under-threat-of-jihadi-violence/a-55690109 (DW)]
